newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Iran wants better OPEC quota checks, no ideas yet.
newsitem.headline: Iran wants better OPEC quota checks, no ideas yet.

text.p: Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh said on Wednesday OPEC's quota compliance committee wanted to find a new mechanism to check member country quota adherence but that no concrete proposals were being considered.
Aghazadeh told reporters after a routine meeting of the ministerial committee in Vienna on Wednesday that the group accepted some member countries were violating allotted quotas.
"We need a mechanism to check members directly...We talked a lot about the matter and how we can make checks and access the correct information and figures," he said.
But Aghazadeh said no firm proposals had yet been made.
And OPEC delegates said there was little OPEC could to police quota compliance other than make appeals for good faith.
With oil markets easily gobbling up current excess supplies, OPEC would best be advised to make the most of current high prices and maintain a low profile on quota violations, the delegates said.
"Nobody wants to rock the boat," said one OPEC delegate in Vienna on Wednesday.
"Not even if we lie down at the wellhead would we be able to say what people are producing," said another. "I can't see anything that will stop the cheaters from cheating."

Meanwhile OPEC linchpin Saudi Arabia has no inclination to take steps to maintain better quota compliance, especially given oil prices already averaging more than $2 a barrel higher than last year, Gulf sources said recently.
Aghazadeh said he believed OPEC needed to find fresh ways of checking because no member country admitted to cheating on quotas and secondary media estimates were not always accurate.
Production figures provided by secondary sources were "not completely correct," he said.
"We feel we have overproduction but don't know exactly (the extent) because nobody accepts they are overproducing and they don't believe the secondary sources."
In June OPEC raised its ceiling to 25.03 million barrels per day (bpd) to allow for the eventual resumption of partial Iraqi exports under a U.N. oil-for-food exchange.
But secondary media sources monitored by OPEC put the group's production in August at 25.77 million bpd, despite the postponement of Iraqi sales, OPEC's Secretariat said last week.
By comparison, according to direct communication from member countries, OPEC averaged 24.72 million bpd in August.
Aghazadeh said Wednesday's meeting also examined ways of trying to maintain current buoyant oil markets which priced benchmark Brent on Wednesday at almost $23 a barrel.
"Now we are satisfied with the price in the market...The main issue is how to continue this price into next year," he said.
Committee members had considered the market situation and price influences such as Iraq, non-OPEC supplies and world economic growth, he said.
Aghazadeh said the quota compliance group would meet again on November 25, two days before OPEC's next full ministerial conference.
The committee also includes Libya's Abdalla al-Badri and Nigeria's Dan Etete and was attended by OPEC Secretary General Rilwanu Lukman.
